name: db3-gripper
description: Legacy .db3 gripper rig, lenient alignment for heavy frame loss
_comment: FREQUENTLY TUNED: the video block below; an explicit CLI flag always wins.
The alignment block is deliberately more permissive than the mcap recipes.
The .db3 generation drops frames heavily and its teleop logic leaves one arm's
joint_cmd silent for whole segments while the other is driven, so the strict
defaults reject nearly every episode. Each relaxation is listed below with what
it costs -- none of them are free, and they all show up in the per-episode audit.
These numbers are a starting point, not a measurement: tighten them once you
have run 'rdp check-rosbag' over a representative batch and know the real drop
notes: joint-state-fill: a silent arm's action columns are copied from its own
measured joints. Those rows teach 'hold the current pose' and nothing else --
audit.hold.joint_state_fill_rows counts them per arm, and the dataset exposes
timestamps/action_hold_mask so training can weight them down.
missing_topic_policy fill: a topic absent for the whole recording is rebuilt
the same way. Check audit.missing_topics before training on such a batch.
invalid_frame_policy drop: rows breaching a tolerance are discarded instead of
failing the episode. audit.dropped_frames says how many; a large number means
the recording, not the tolerance, is the problem.
max_tick_rate_deviation 0.25: accepts an anchor camera running 22.5-37.5 Hz
against --fps 30. The LeRobot timestamp column is frame_index/fps, so anything
accepted here is real clock drift in the dataset.
max_hold_fraction 0.6: still rejects an episode that is mostly held action,
which is the failure mode this leniency would otherwise hide.
